priorStories.headline: Russian drone barrage cuts power across Ukraine
priorStories.body:
Russia launched 433 drones at Ukraine from Saturday evening into Sunday, according to Ukraine’s air force, which said 371 were destroyed or suppressed.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attacks left hundreds of thousands of households without electricity. Ukrainian authorities also said a drone strike at a vocational-school site in the Vinnytsia region killed three people, including a 13-year-old girl.

priorStories.headline: U.N. ends Western Sahara mission after 35 years
priorStories.body:
The United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara ceased operations after the Security Council failed to renew its mandate. A smaller support team will oversee its liquidation.

Established in 1991, the mission monitored the disputed territory and supported a ceasefire between Morocco and the Polisario Front.

candidates.summary: The Trump administration filed an emergency Supreme Court appeal seeking to segregate about 20,000 California mail ballots from voters it suspects may not be citizens while their eligibility is checked. California officials say the federal list is unreliable and includes citizens; lower courts rejected the request, warning that it could disrupt the November 3 midterm election and disenfranchise eligible voters.
candidates.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to segregate disputed California ballots

candidates.summary: Uganda's military announced that it had begun a phased withdrawal of its peacekeeping troops from Somalia under a bilateral agreement with Somali authorities. A military spokesperson said the first contingent had returned to Uganda and that thousands remained deployed; all Ugandan troops are expected to leave by the end of 2027.
candidates.title: Uganda announces phased withdrawal of troops from Somalia

candidates.summary: Iran said its seven-step proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming nuclear negotiations with the United States could be condensed into two days if Washington met its conditions. Iranian officials said contacts through mediators remained active, but the latest Qatari-mediated discussions had ended without a breakthrough.
candidates.title: Iran outlines shortened plan for reopening Strait of Hormuz
candidates.geography: Iran; United States; Qatar; Strait of Hormuz

candidates.summary: World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said reported attacks in northern Ethiopia had killed civilians, including children, and warned that the region's health system was nearing collapse. Tedros did not give dates or casualty totals for the cited attacks or identify the perpetrators; he said insecurity was obstructing medical deliveries.
candidates.title: WHO chief warns northern Ethiopia health system is nearing collapse

candidates.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's emergency request to segregate about 20,000 California mail ballots from voters it alleged might not be citizens. The court gave no reasoning. California officials said the federal list contained extensive errors and separating the ballots immediately before the November 3 midterm election could disenfranchise eligible voters.
candidates.title: Supreme Court rejects request to segregate disputed California ballots

candidates.summary: The British government announced plans to extend the standard qualifying period for permanent residency on work visas from five to 10 years. Doctors, nurses, teachers, care workers meeting an income threshold, and people earning at least £50,000 would retain five-year routes, while some higher earners could qualify sooner. The government said the changes would be introduced during 2027.
candidates.title: Britain announces longer permanent-residency pathway for many immigrants

candidates.summary: Federal and local authorities announced Operation Deep Cover, an increased law-enforcement response in Dallas' Deep Ellum entertainment district, after three shootings there early Sunday killed four people and injured 15. Dallas police said they were investigating whether the shootings were related and pursuing possible suspects.
candidates.title: Authorities announce increased policing after deadly Dallas shootings

candidates.summary: Iran said its seven-step proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming nuclear negotiations with the United States could be implemented within two days if Washington met its conditions. Earlier talks with Qatari mediators ended without a breakthrough, but Qatari mediators traveled to Tehran on Monday night to discuss a draft agreement with Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi. Vice President JD Vance said the countries had made some progress toward a negotiated settlement.
candidates.title: Qatari mediators return to Tehran after Iran outlines two-day Hormuz plan
candidates.geography: Iran; United States; Qatar; Strait of Hormuz

candidates.summary: The United States carried out limited strikes on Iranian targets on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to U.S. officials. One official said Iranian surface-to-air missile positions threatening U.S. assets were targeted. Iranian state media reported explosions on the island. U.S. Central Command had not publicly announced the operation at the time of the reports.
candidates.title: United States carries out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
candidates.geography: United States; Iran; Strait of Hormuz

candidates.summary: New York state and Lewis County health officials announced that a child had died in association with an ongoing measles outbreak. Officials described it as New York's first known measles-associated death in more than 30 years. The state reported 178 measles cases through October 24 and urged residents to check that they were current on measles, mumps and rubella vaccinations.
candidates.title: New York reports first measles-associated death in more than 30 years
candidates.geography: United States; New York; Lewis County

sources.name: New York State Department of Health

candidates.summary: Ukrainian authorities said Russian bombing of an aid distribution center and a neighboring shelter in the southern Kherson region killed 26 people. The attacks followed the expiration of a limited ceasefire that had allowed aid deliveries and evacuations in front-line and Russian-occupied areas.
candidates.title: Russian attacks on aid center and shelter kill 26 in southern Ukraine, officials say
